newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Lebed denies coup talk, to sue rival - Interfax.
newsitem.headline: Lebed denies coup talk, to sue rival - Interfax.

text.p: Russian security chief Alexander Lebed on Wednesday dismissed allegations he was planning to seize power and said he would sue Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov for making the accusations.
"There can be no talk of a mutiny," Lebed told Interfax news agency. Asked to explain Kulikov's charges, Lebed replied sarcastically: "The poor thing has got everything wrong."
Lebed, Kulikov and other top officials are involved in a fierce Kremlin power struggle which has worsened since President Boris Yeltsin announced on September 5 that he planned to have heart surgery.

"For the first time in my life I am planning to go to court, to sue Alexander Kulikov. I don't need the money he has obtained through bribes, and therefore I will ask for damages of one rouble. I will win this rouble and treasure it as a souvenir," Lebed told Interfax.
Kulikov accused Lebed of planning to set up an elite legion to combat civil unrest and said the security chief was setting up his own power structures.

But Lebed said it was no secret he had asked the interior and defence ministries to set up a single brigade of 3,000 to 3,500 people to ensure "there would be some kind of power in the state". He said the two ministries had told him they could do so by the end of 1999.
